Kimberly / Marissa —

Quick read of the ask: NeuroSynth looks strategic (large healthcare dataset use case, potential multi-year expansion). Aditya's numbers show a big short-term token spike but predictable tiering afterwards. I think we can offer a smoothing credit rather than a flat discount to avoid resetting pricing expectations. Proposed approach:

- Offer a one-time smoothing credit equal to 30% of billed usage for months 1–3 (applied as a pre-paid credit against invoices) AND 20% off list for months 4–12, conditional on a 12-month minimum commitment and a committed MRR floor of $75k.
- Require standard VPC cost pass-through and a one-time setup fee to cover network engineering.
- Amend SOW to include rollback to standard rates if usage drops below 50% of the committed floor in any two consecutive quarters.

This reduces immediate revenue impact relative to a straight 40% off list, preserves some unit economics, and gives us an expansion path.

That said, the combined revenue impact is non-trivial — we should get CFO sign-off. Attaching a quick model of the revenue impact assuming the profile in Aditya's sheet.

Attachments: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (highlighted change set)

Can you review and, if agreeable, I will request formal CFO signoff and prepare an amendment template?

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

Markus / Marissa,

I reviewed the numbers against Q3 forecast and ran sensitivity for adoption/expansion. Short summary:

- If NeuroSynth ramps as Aditya projects, the one-time smoothing credit + stepped discount yields ~ $720k recognized revenue over 12 months vs $1.14M at list — an incremental gross margin reduction of roughly $280k (assumes VPC pass-through).
- The largest downside is the front-loaded credit (months 1–3). If we move to a deferred credit (applied over months 1–6) we reduce churn exposure but extend margin pressure.
- Legal requests tighter commitments (12 months + MRR floor) and a DocuSign amendment.

My recommendation for approval boundary: finance can approve up to a 25% effective concession (across credits + discounts) for strategic pilots. Anything larger — like the proposed 30% front credit — needs CFO signoff.

I'm attaching the workbook with the scenarios.

Attachments: finance_impact_q3.xlsx
